name: Bariga
blurb: The neighborhood that names the origin story — Wo was shot here; in July 2025 the LCDA renamed Ajidagan Street "Olamide Adedeji (Baddo) Street" and re-christened the Charly Boy bus stop for him. Every era still points back to these streets.

name: Agege
blurb: Where shaku shaku lived before Wo pushed it into national choreography.

name: Yaba / Coded Tunes
blurb: The small Yoruba-rap label orbit that signed him — before YBNL, before the empire.

name: Ijebu-Ode — TASUED
blurb: Tai Solarin University of Education, where he read mass communication before the dropout that the whole origin story pivots on — the certificate traded for Coded Tunes, then everything after.

name: Ikeja — Police College, Ikeja GRA
blurb: New Year's Day 2026: the Mainland Block Party "Mission 26K" headline show at the Police College, Ikeja GRA — roughly 30,000 billed, the Street King opening the year on the Mainland, decades after clearing the same corridor's radio and TV rooms.

name: OLIC — Eko Hotel & Teslim Balogun Stadium
blurb: Olamide Live in Concert — the series that made the Street King run flesh. OLIC launched 28 December 2014 at Eko Hotel & Suites and ran there again in 2015, 2016 and 2018; OLIC 4 stepped up to Teslim Balogun Stadium, Surulere on 17 December 2017, a stadium-scale bet that press coverage noted drew under expectations — the ambition, not the turnout, is the archive point.

name: Lagos Island stages
blurb: Award shows, TV freestyles, and the industry rooms that first had to make space for Yoruba street bars.

name: Lagos
blurb: The city that is the soundtrack — from Bariga corners to national charts, every chapter is a Lagos chapter.

name: Ibadan
blurb: Yoruba heartland stops with receipts: the Glo Mega Music Show stormed the University of Ibadan (2015), Phyno-and-Olamide campus bills ran before it, and the city even owns a song — "Ibadan," cut with Qdot. The language of the records meeting the language of the crowd.

name: Abuja
blurb: Capital-city stages on the Street King and label-boss tours — the archive's national reach, not just coastal. The April 2018 Kings Meet bill that packed Moscow's Palace of Gymnastics was billed on the same tour pages as these Abuja-season dates.

name: Enugu
blurb: Phyno's home city — the eastern pole of the 2 Kings negotiation, and the peer-rap axis that kept the run from being Lagos-only.

name: Accra
blurb: West African circuit stop with receipts: the Ghana Meets Naija stage in 2016, and "Wonders" with Shatta Wale performed at BF Suma's anniversary in Accra the same year — street-hop and Afrobeats trading stages across the coast.

name: London
blurb: 23 November 2025: sold out OVO Arena Wembley — reported as the first Nigerian rapper to fill the 12,000-cap room. On the back of it, a headline O2 Arena show was announced for 25 March 2027, billed as a first for a Nigerian act. The diaspora stage became the destination.

name: Paris
blurb: European Afrobeats corridor — festival and club bills that carried the catalog beyond Anglophone rooms.

name: New York
blurb: 11 May 2018: the USA Culture Tour opener — the first push of the catalog onto American showcase rooms, years before the Empire-era bills that made New York a repeat stop.

name: Toronto
blurb: North American diaspora stop — the Mainland Block Party brand's New Year show was reported here via social channels (billed like the Ikeja Mission 26K); the archive holds the pin as a corridor marker, not a confirmed date.

name: Johannesburg
blurb: Southern Africa's pin is the label's, not the founder's — yet. The documented moment on file is Asake's solo Johannesburg debut (3 January 2026, Goldrush Dome), the second generation carrying YBNL into the continent's streaming boom before Olamide's own stage there is booked.
